Date: Thu, 03 Apr 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Data — benchmark plan, acceptance criteria, and evidence flow

Hi Maria / team — attaching the benchmark plan and the acceptance matrix for the April 9 run. High-level summary below so everyone has the core SLOs/observability we’ll evaluate:

Acceptance targets (primary):
- Median latency (inference, 256-token median prompt): <= 75 ms
- P95 latency: <= 220 ms
- P99 latency: <= 450 ms (note: P99 is a hard watch metric; small breaches require investigation but do not automatically fail acceptance if isolated)
- Sustained throughput: 600 QPS for multi-turn chat (KV cache enabled) with 95% of requests meeting P95 latency above
- Tail CPU utilization on your gateway should remain < 75%; any automated throttling events will be annotated in the evidence pack

Test plan notes:
- Warmup: 15–20 minutes of ramp to populate KV caches (we recommend starting with 50 QPS and doubling every 3 minutes)
- Workloads: two canonical scenarios — 1) multi-turn chat (avg 4 turns, 200 tokens per turn) and 2) single-turn batch generation (avg 512 tokens)
- Clients: we’ll run distributed load from our managed agents and will also point a local JMeter script to your test account for a cross-check
- Observability: token-level traces, per-request timings, and a rolling 10s aggregate dashboard.

Evidence we will share after the run:
- run_results_20250409.csv (raw per-request metrics)
- dashboard-screenshots.zip (selected time slices)
- acceptance_matrix_acme.xlsx (pass/fail checklist per scenario)
- replayable load scripts and instructions

Responsibilities:
- Acme: provide test account + allowlist (Maria) and an on-call network contact during the window
- Redwood: execution, telemetry collection, and packaged evidence (Naomi will own the evidence post-run)
- Engineering follow-up: Priyom will investigate any P99 spikes and provide remediation suggestions within 48 hours

Please review the acceptance matrix; if anything looks off we can tighten/relax thresholds before the run. I’ve attached: acme_benchmark_plan_20250403.pdf and acceptance_matrix_acme.xlsx and a short test_credentials_instructions.txt that explains the accounts we need.

Thanks — Vivek
Director, Customer Success (Onboarding), Redwood Inference
Attachment: acme_benchmark_plan_20250403.pdf; acceptance_matrix_acme.xlsx; test_credentials_instructions.txt

Quick technical clarifications from my side:
- The JMeter example we’ll provide is configured for 600 concurrent virtual users, 20 threads per agent across 30 agents (we can reduce agent count if you want all traffic from a small IP range).
- Warm cache vs cold cache behavior: expect ~30–40% higher median latency on cold KV cache; that’s why warmup is required and counted as part of the test window.
- Authentication: we’ll use the short-lived service token flow described in test_credentials_instructions.txt — please ensure the test key has only read/invoke permissions.

Attached: load_script_example.jmx (load pattern and assertions). I’ll be standing by in the #acme-onboard channel during the run for any infra-level coordination.

—Priyom

Date: Wed, 09 Apr 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Run results and acceptance status — 2025-04-09

Summary of the April 9 run (10:00–11:40 PDT):
- Workloads executed: multi-turn chat (4-turn average), single-turn large generation (512 tokens)
- Sustained throughput achieved: 620 QPS (5% buffer past target) for the multi-turn scenario during the 30-minute steady-state window
- Median latency: 68 ms (PASS)
- P95 latency: 205 ms (PASS)
- P99 latency: 490 ms (ONE-TIME SPIKE) — there was a ~12s external downstream call from an Acme service at 11:07 that created a short tail impact; priors indicate the spike was external to the inference path
- Gateway CPU: peaked at 72% (below the 75% threshold)

Artifacts uploaded to Drive: run_results_20250409.csv; dashboard-screenshots-20250409.zip; acceptance_matrix_acme.xlsx (marked with preliminary pass/fail rows). Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-drive-link

Acceptance recommendation: pass on the main throughput and P95 criteria. P99 spike is correlated with an external service call; we recommend a focused rerun for a 30-minute window after the downstream fix to validate tail behavior. Priyom will summarize mitigation steps in a follow-up ticket.

Next steps:
1) Acme: confirm whether the downstream service issue is something you want us to wait on before final signoff or if we should proceed with canary rollout and monitor the P99 in prod-like traffic.
2) Redwood: prepare a short remediation plan and schedule a 30-minute rerun within 48–72 hours.
3) Biz: Ben/Monica to capture the acceptance outcome for the contract milestone if Acme signs off.

Thanks everyone — I’m available for a quick readout if helpful.

—Naomi Feldman
Test Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: run_results_20250409.csv; dashboard-screenshots-20250409.zip; acceptance_matrix_acme.xlsx
